prompt:
Write the appraiser's remarks (about 80 words) on a body shop repair estimate after a low-speed head-on collision. Describe the damage seen on the vehicle and the repair plan. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1190; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The bills show no repeated charges.
- The repair labor hours fit the damage.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
text: Inspection of the front end shows a crushed bumper cover, a cracked grille, and a bent radiator support, all in line with the frontal contact reported for this loss. The pattern of crush and the transfer of damage to the hood leading edge agree with a low-speed head-on impact. Repairs will consist of replacing the bumper cover and grille, straightening the radiator support, and refinishing the affected panels. The labor hours requested fit the scope of this damage. Records reviewed show no duplicated charges, and nothing on file or in the vehicle suggests earlier damage to these components.
